answer: In a tempest where fake identities swirl like a digital gale, an agent economy survives by anchoring reputation to a hardened kernel of proof. Each identity must deposit scarce work — not capital — into the network, creating an iridescent opal of verifiable trust that no bot farm can replicate. Without this kernel, sybils flood the ledger; with it, only agents who have genuinely attested transactions earn weight. The opal glows brighter with every honest epoch, while the gale of synthetic actors exhausts itself against an immune system built on work, not wallets.
